name: Addressing
definition: Following \cite{maass1992lower}, let $r=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$. The addressing class has $n$ concepts on a domain consisting of $n$ address points and $r$ bit points: the concept indexed by $i\in[n]$ is positive on address point $i$ and, on the bit points, equals a fixed injective $r$-bit encoding of $i$. In particular it combines a singleton family with its binary address.
comments: The encoding is part of this family and is not required to contain every r-bit word. Complete-code benchmark values are explicitly scoped to $n=2^r$. For other n, encoding-dependent parameters can differ; see survey Proposition \ref{prop:addressing-encoding-scope}. The database definition is authoritative, including its n indexed concepts and r=ceil(log2 n) bit coordinates.
